- Accounting Automation: What It Is and Why It Matters


Accounting automation is the use of AI software and automation tools to replace manual, repetitive tasks like data entry, bank reconciliation, payroll administration, and basic tax prep and filing.[Adoption is already widespread](https://kpmg.com/us/en/articles/2024/ai-in-finance-us-report.html) : most companies (88%) have brought AI-powered tools into their finance function, and 76% are piloting or using them specifically for accounting.


For firms, automation in accounting is designed to help faster growth, fewer costly errors, and real-time visibility into financial health. For employees, it is designed to help free up time once spent on manual work so they can focus on higher-value advisory services instead.


Automation does not eliminate the need for human judgment and oversight. Accounting automation is reshaping how accountants work, but it’s built to support them, not replace the empathy and judgment only a person can bring.


## **Key Points**


- Accounting automation covers technologies like agentic AI and intelligent document processing that handle manual, everyday tasks such as data entry and bank reconciliations.
- The automation of accounting processes can free up hours of accountants’ time for higher-value work like client consulting and advisory. Even just automating data entry can help significantly cut time spent crunching data.


- Top benefits of accounting automation include improved accuracy/error reduction, greater scalability and time savings.
- Many companies are piloting or using AI and automation tools today. But while many accounting workflows can be automated, ones requiring human judgment cannot.


## **What is Accounting Automation?**


Accounting automation is the software and AI-driven tools that take over repetitive, rules-based accounting tasks. This includes everyday processes like data entry and reporting.[Core technologies](https://www.intuit.com/blog/innovative-thinking/accounting-technology/) used in the automation of accounting processes are:


- **Intelligent document processing (IDP):** IDP can automatically handle invoice extraction, capture purchase order data, process expense reports, and more.
- **Robotic process automation (RPA):** These bots are programmed to handle simple, repetitive tasks and workflows. This includes bookkeeping, AP/AR, payroll, invoicing, and expense management. RPA bots don’t learn the way more advanced systems do.
- **Machine learning (ML):** These AI systems analyze and learn from large datasets, making them useful in predictive decision-making processes. ML software can also handle tasks like invoice extraction/processing and bank reconciliation.
- **Agentic AI:** Agentic AI builds on generative AI, adding the ability to plan, take action, and adjust based on results rather than just respond to a prompt. In accounting, it can investigate and help solve problems in real time, automating processes like tax compliance and data entry. The technology is still in the early adoption phase, as it’s still relatively unpredictable and unregulated.


Studies show that over[75% of companies](https://kpmg.com/kpmg-us/content/dam/kpmg/pdf/2024/audit/ai-in-finance-us-report-dec-2024.pdf) are piloting or using AI and automation tools. The accounting software market alone is worth over[$20 billion](https://www.researchandmarkets.com/reports/5767672/accounting-software-market-report) with an anticipated compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 13.4%.


Automation in accounting is becoming increasingly widespread, and for good reason. Manual accounting work is repetitive and leaves room for human error, which can be costly to businesses. It’s also time-consuming, keeping accountants from prioritizing higher-value tasks, like client advisory services.


## **How Automation Works in the Accounting Process**


The automation of accounting processes facilitates everyday accounting practices, whether that’s generating financial statements or recording transactions. It frees up time and can help reduce costs for the firm, while enabling greater scalability. The way it works is simple.


The software connects to existing systems so data can flow automatically between them. This can be done in real time or on a preset schedule. Using AI rules, the software then analyzes and categorizes every transaction. If it finds any discrepancies or anomalies, it flags them for human review.


While the AI handles routine accounting processes, the team can focus on other matters. Whenever something comes up requiring human oversight or judgment calls, they’ll step in to handle it.


### **Common Accounting Tasks Ready for Automation**


In the accounting industry, automation can be an effective tool for saving money and time. Even just using it to automate data entry can save accountants roughly[six hours a week](https://www.accountingtoday.com/news/59-of-accountants-use-ai-to-save-about-30-hours-a-week-on-tasks) . And that’s before counting other time-saving opportunities.


Besides data entry, accountants are using automation for things like:


- **Accounts payable/accounts receivable—** Process and route invoices to the correct department, flag mistakes and duplicates, match payments to open invoices, and address invoicing disputes
- **Bank reconciliation—** Verify payments across internal records and bank statements, auto-match transactions, flag exceptions, and provide real-time reconciliations for continuous visibility into financials
- **Expense management—** Track, analyze, categorize, and report on company expenses to ensure accurate financial reporting and reduce fraud risk
- **Tax prep support—** Handle routine data entry tasks, cross-reference tax forms against internal records, flag discrepancies, identify credits/deductions, and track regulatory changes to help ensure compliance


The[best AI accounting software](https://www.intuit.com/blog/innovative-thinking/best-ai-accounting-software-tools/) can save firms time and money. QuickBooks with Intuit Intelligence, for example, can support automated insights, reporting, and reconciliation in one place. Consider options carefully before integrating any new tech into your workflows.


## **Benefits of Accounting Automation**


Core benefits of accounting automation are:


- **Time savings:**[McKinsey](https://www.mckinsey.com/mgi/our-research/a-new-future-of-work-the-race-to-deploy-ai-and-raise-skills-in-europe-and-beyond) projects up to 30% of US work hours could be automated by 2030 as AI adoption accelerates. With less time being spent on these tasks (e.g., data entry or invoice processing), accountants can focus on more strategic work.
- **Accuracy/error reduction:** Accounting automation helps cut down on human error, which can be costly to fix.[Ardent Partners’ research](https://www.bottomline.com/download_file/84ec3c2a-cc1b-4d5d-8457-ce18d337b7b4/1547) puts the average cost of a manually processed invoice at $12.88, with best-in-class accounts payable teams bringing that down to $2.78 through automation.
- **Scalability:** AI-powered systems don’t have the same time and energy limitations as humans. This allows them to handle routine work at scale, which enables firms to grow more quickly. With automation, employees can also use their own ingenuity to provide greater value to clients.


If you’re looking to[grow your accounting firm](https://www.intuit.com/blog/innovative-thinking/accounting-firm-growth-strategy/) , automation is certainly one strategy. Investing in the tech that scales with you without burdening your team can mean faster decision-making and better insights so you can better serve your clients.


## **The Impact of Automation on the Accounting Industry**


The impact of automation in the accounting industry can’t be ignored. After all,[76% of companies’ finance teams](https://kpmg.com/us/en/articles/2024/ai-in-finance-us-report.html) are already using AI-powered solutions (and automation tools) for accounting purposes. More are expected to adopt AI in the future as well.


That said,[automation is not replacing accountants](https://www.intuit.com/blog/innovative-thinking/will-ai-replace-accountants/) . Rather, it’s changing the way these professionals work.


No longer do accountants have to spend a large portion of their days on routine tasks like data entry or reporting. Thanks to[accounting innovations](https://www.intuit.com/blog/innovative-thinking/innovation-in-accounting/) like AI copilots and automation, that time is being shifted to more strategic work. This includes client advisory services and exception-handling. These are areas that require creative thinking, empathy, and human judgment, which AI just can’t do.


Besides, as useful as automation tools are, they’re not perfect. Human oversight is still needed to ensure correct setup and implementation. Teams also need to be trained in how these systems work to ensure optimal efficiency. And since AI can make mistakes, ongoing testing and review are also necessary.


Ultimately, AI-powered tools are at their best when handling structured, repetitive work. Anything requiring actual, experience-based judgment or regulatory interpretation falls to the people.


## **Start Automating Your Accounting Today**


AI-powered solutions are rapidly evolving. So, those in the accounting industry should continue to expect big changes going forward.


Already, automation can handle repetitive accounting workflows at scale. For many manual processes like accounts reconciliation or transaction categorization. This frees up time for the employees and saves money for the firm.

## **FAQs**


###


Accounting automation technologies are best-suited to routine, repetitive processes. For example, robotic process automation (RPA) can handle things like data entry and accounts payable/receivable. It can also automate bank reconciliations and prepare invoices. More advanced tools, like machine learning, can even support decision-making processes.


###


Automated accounting software can usually integrate well with existing business applications, like a CRM or eComm platform. This allows data to flow automatically between them so the team has access to everything all at once. The software follows AI logic to automate accounting workflows, like invoice processing. It also flags any anomalies for the team to review and resolve.


###


According to[KPMG](https://kpmg.com/us/en/articles/2024/ai-in-finance-us-report.html) , 88% of financial services companies have adopted AI solutions. But the successful adoption of accounting automation tools requires change management and clean, standardized data. After all, the tool is only as good as the data it’s given. Automation tools also aren’t great with exception handling, which is where human judgment is crucial.


###


The best way to measure productivity and accuracy is to check the data. Approximately[81% of accountants](https://www.firmofthefuture.com/news/accountant-tech-survey-2025/) say AI tools boost their productivity. This is primarily through workflow automation, which saves professionals hours of routine work each week. Review the numbers to find out how many errors were being made (and how much time was being spent) prior to implementation versus now.
